title: Fiancée and the Slave Trader
text: “Hm?”
Surely this flow of events couldn’t mean what I thought it meant!?
“What is it? Castle soldiers?”
Ren was delivering lines that should’ve been Keel’s. How comical, that someone who merely resembled her closely was standing in for her, I say.
“It’s that circus caravan that’s been getting famous lately! Our princess has taken a great interest and granted an audience!”

Since the Saint’s activities were all being conducted underground, none of the credit was going to Father. If anything, it was Rafumi, disguised as Ren, who was pulling most of the strings behind the scenes.
“Princess…?”
“Spare me. Are we really about to have that woman’s hideous face paraded in front of us here?”

Father and Ren muttered this in weary tones from inside the carriage. Itsuki narrowed his eyes with a look that said “no comment.” It was the expression of someone who had already given up entirely on that Crimson Swine. Reluctantly, Father peered through the gap in the carriage curtains to check on the other party’s carriage.
“A princess, you say? Someone so exalted, coming to speak with the likes of us?”
“Indeed. You should consider it an honor beyond your station.”

A Siltvelt envoy stepped forward as the negotiator. And, unsurprisingly, the attitude was every bit as high-handed as one might expect. Still… given how this princess was making her entrance, surely it couldn’t be the Crimson Swine. Even I hadn’t expected to run into that pig here, of all places.
“Motoyasu-kun, do you know anything about this?”
“For now, best to watch how things unfold, I say. Pay close attention to the princess’s name.”
“A-alright.”
Father relayed this quietly to the Siltvelt envoy who had just stepped back.
“So? What sort of person is this princess? I’d like to hear her name.”
“Listen well and be humbled. The one who graces us is Melromarc’s second princess, Lady Melty Melromarc.”
So it was Fiancée after all. Given Rafumi’s attitude and the timing, I’d suspected as much all along.
“Um…”
“Never heard that name. Must be a different person from that princess.”
“I feel like I’ve heard it somewhere. Didn’t that princess have a younger sister who didn’t get along with her…?”
“Eclair-san!”

Father called out, summoning Éclair from a carriage further back. Ah, right, she’d been here all along. Éclair, who in the loop where we’d stayed in Melromarc had died in prison, had already been taken under our protection. If we arranged a face-to-face meeting here, would things go more smoothly?
“I don’t understand the situation at all—coming to pay respects to what’s ostensibly just an ordinary circus troupe.”
We weren’t even famous as the Sacred Bird’s Saint here, and yet the Three Heroes Church was maneuvering behind the scenes to drag Fiancée out to a place like this. Just what were they scheming?
“I feel like I heard this from Motoyasu-kun before… wasn’t she the one who got along well with Filo-chan, or something like that?”
“More or less correct, indeed. Ah, she’s bound to get swept up in some conspiracy, so you Heroes had better guard her properly, or there’ll be trouble.”

Rafumi delivered this warning with an air of great self-importance. Ren and Itsuki both bristled at the tone. Left out of the loop entirely, the slaves behind us were tightening their guard. Or rather—with this many people around, plotting to assassinate a princess here would be beyond foolish, wouldn’t it? In a period when soldiers were already scarce enough to require conscription, and with the Waves drawing near, causing an incident like this now made no sense whatsoever. I simply couldn’t fathom what those people were thinking.
“She’s a princess of this country, you know?”
“In a bad way, that inspires zero confidence.”

“As far as trustworthiness goes, that’s one area where even I can vouch for the person in question, I say. There’s a risk she might get aroused if she plays her role too idealistically, but at heart she never does anything to harm Father and the others, and she gets along splendidly with Filo-tan. In a sense, she remains my rival in love to this very day.”
“I don’t quite get it, but is she some kind of pervert on Motoyasu-kun’s level?”
“Naofumi… you say some things, you really do.”
“Just being that princess’s younger sister already disqualifies her, if you ask me.”
Itsuki declared this with a thoroughly dismissive attitude.
“I heard Lady Melty has arrived!”
Éclair came running up. Meanwhile, that fiancée of mine had already brazenly hopped down from her carriage and was calling out not just to Filo-tan but to the Filolial-samas in general.
“Filolials?”
“Hmm?”
“P-Princess!”

And with that, she reached out and gently stroked Filo-tan’s face. Filo-tan, being stroked, narrowed her eyes as though it felt wonderful. Heh… Fiancée. That one there ought to be Rafumi. After all, whenever I go in for a hug, it always turns out to be Rafumi with a puff of smoke.
“I’d heard there was a caravan going around trying to lift Melromarc’s gloomy mood, pulled by some strange bird monster—so it really is a Filolial after all.”
“Hmm… loo~ser?”
“Y-you can talk?”
Hmm… this brought back memories of the loop where we’d stayed in Melromarc, and Fiancée’s exchanges tangled up with Sakura-chan. This time it was Filo-tan. Presumed to be Rafumi, though.
“Yup! Filo can talk—everyone here can talk too!”
“Wow… talking with a Filolial has been my dream! Tell me more… about yourself.”

“Sure! Filo’s name is Filo! And that one over there is Kou, and the one glaring daggers at the Sword Dog over there is Luna—ah, Luna needs to run things by our leader Yuki first, Yuki gets really cranky about it—when I said ‘loser’ she got super mad at me—”
“Is ‘loser’ just your catchphrase, then?”
“When I say it, Rafumi gives me chocolate—loo~ser—”
Fiancée was chatting away with Filo-tan, looking thoroughly delighted.
“Filo’s job is helping Master by pulling the carriage, but everyone pulls it together!”
“Is that so? I came here today to have an important talk with your master. I hope we can build a good relationship from here.”
“Hmm…”
“H-hey, may I pet you a little more?”
“Sure! Luna’s chest is even fluffier, though. Ah, but Master takes care of everyone’s feathers, so maybe everyone’s fluffy?”
“Even so, let me pet you.”
“Okay!”
Grr… Rafumi! Just how long do you intend to keep pretending to be Filo-tan!? Or do you actually mean to insist that’s the genuine Filo-tan!?
“Those Filolials are gathering around with absolutely no caution at all.”
“It’s a heartwarming sight, isn’t it.”
“Wait, is Luna targeting me!?”
Ren tensed up, on high alert. That’s just an initiation rite, that.
“Ufufu… Filo-chan, thank you. My name is Melty.”
“You’re welcome—Mel-chan!”
Fiancée and Filo-tan began to settle into a cheerful atmosphere together.
“From what I can see, she doesn’t seem like a bad kid. Should be fine.”
Father climbed down from the carriage and approached Fiancée.
“That child… did she take a liking to Filo, I wonder?”
“Yes! Ah…”
When Father spoke to her, his face hidden beneath his hood, Fiancée snapped to attention and gave a bow.
“Princess!”
Éclair arrived alongside Crocodile Guy, offering a salute and bowing her head toward Fiancée.
“How dare you—shameless—”
“Stop that!”
A knight tried to step in, and Fiancée cut him off sharply. The knight glared at Fiancée with an expression of pure resentment.
“Princess Melty! I, Eclair Seaetto, have defied the kingdom’s orders. Please forgive my insolence in appearing before you.”
“This matter has been taken quite seriously by Mother as well. I’ve been entrusted with a message on this front too—that your circumstances are to be treated as unquestioned.”
“Oh… such generous words. You have my deepest thanks.”
At Fiancée’s words, the eyebrows of a nearby knight twitched violently with displeasure.
“That matter is important, but the main business is here.”
Saying so, Fiancée cast a glance at Éclair, silently asking who among them served as representative. Éclair, taking the cue, turned her face toward Father as the representative.
“My name is Melty Melromarc. Please forgive us for having to make this visit in such a place, of all things.”

For this loop, I absolutely had to prevent Father from building an excessively good relationship with her as some ideal Hero figure. Well, since Father was busy running the circus and tending to the slaves this time around, he probably wouldn’t have the leisure to play the prince-charming role like he had before, so it should be fine. Still, I could recall it even now—that face Fiancée had worn, like a maiden smitten, gazing at Father. Hey, Rafumi, surely you’re not scheming to have Fiancée be the one to relieve Father of his virginity, are you? I’ll stop that without fail. I won’t hand Father over to Fiancée any more than I’d hand over Filo-tan!
